memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Anyone who kidnaps someone is to be put to death, whether the victim has been sold or is still in the kidnapper's possession." - Exodus 21:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Long before the modern world named the horror of human trafficking, God had already condemned it in the strongest terms. To steal a person, to sell a human being as though they were cattle, was among the gravest of crimes. A person is not property to be seized and traded. This single verse cuts against the entire slave-trading enterprise that scarred human history — God had already declared it worthy of death.

This tells us something precious about how God views people. You are not a commodity. You cannot be reduced to a price tag, however the world tries. Every person carries a dignity given by God that no one has the right to steal or sell.

And there is gospel here too. We were once held captive, not by a kidnapper, but by sin and death. Yet Jesus came to redeem us — the word means to buy back — not to trade us away but to set us free at the cost of His own blood (1 Pet 1:18-19). The God who forbade the stealing of persons is the God who purchased us to make us His own beloved children.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I truly believe I am valued by God, not defined by any earthly price?
How can I stand up for the dignity and freedom of others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see every person as precious, never as property. Thank You for redeeming me at great cost, and stir my heart to defend the freedom and worth of others. Amen.
